answer: Each agent carries a signed beacon token issued by a trusted registrar that records its cumulative work as a velvet‑hashed ledger entry. When voting, the protocol applies quadratic weighting: an identity’s influence is the square root of its token stake, so a swarm of pearls—many low‑stake identities—contributes far less than a single high‑stake node. An attacker must therefore acquire or forge tokens worth the square of the desired influence, making the cost grow quadratically with impact.
